# The local package repository

This page is for administrators and hosting teams who look into `var/storage/packages/`, copy packages between
servers, or prepare an installation without network access. It answers: where packages are kept, how the
directories are named, what each one is for, and what you may touch.

## Contents

1. [Where it is](#where-it-is)
2. [The layout](#the-layout)
3. [How a vendor directory is chosen](#how-a-vendor-directory-is-chosen)
4. [The local repository and the system repository](#the-local-repository-and-the-system-repository)
5. [The .cache directory](#the-cache-directory)
6. [An offline index.xml](#an-offline-indexxml)
7. [What you may do by hand](#what-you-may-do-by-hand)
8. [Related pages](#related-pages)

## Where it is

`eZPackage::repositoryPath()` builds the path from three parts:

```text
var / site.ini [FileSettings] StorageDir / package.ini [RepositorySettings] RepositoryDirectory
var / storage                            / packages
```

The first part is the literal `var`; the repository does not move with `[FileSettings] VarDir`. As shipped
(`StorageDir=storage`, `RepositoryDirectory=packages`) it is `var/storage/packages/` below the installation root, for
every siteaccess. A new installation may not have the directory yet; the kernel then lists no repository besides
`local`.

## The layout

```text
var/storage/packages/
├── 7x/                              vendor "7x": the setup wizard's system repository
│   ├── index.xml                    optional: the offline index (see below)
│   ├── sevenx_multisite/
│   │   ├── package.xml
│   │   ├── .cache/package.php       the kernel's parsed copy, not part of the package
│   │   ├── documents/  files/  settings/
│   ├── sevenx_classes/
│   └── sevenx_multisite_democontent/
├── ez-systems/                      vendor "eZ systems"
│   └── ezstarrating_extension/
├── local/                           packages without a vendor, and new packages from the wizards
└── dryrun/                          only during a kickstarter dry run, removed afterwards
```

Every directory directly below `var/storage/packages/` is a **repository**; every directory in a repository that holds
a `package.xml` or `package.json` is a **package** (`eZPackage::packageRepositories()`, `fetchPackages()`). Its
directory name is the package's `<name>`. On a fresh `sevenx_multisite` installation the `7x` repository holds
`sevenx_multisite`, `sevenx_classes` and `sevenx_multisite_democontent`.

## How a vendor directory is chosen

| Package | Repository |
|---|---|
| Imported, with a `<vendor>` | the vendor run through the `urlalias` transformation: `7x` stays `7x`, `eZ systems` becomes `ez-systems` |
| Imported, without a `<vendor>` | `local` |
| Imported with an explicit repository (`ezpm import` with `-r`, a kickstarter dry run) | that repository |
| Created by a wizard or `ezpm create` | `local` (`eZPackage::create()`: "New packages always use local repository") |

Two packages of the same name in two repositories can exist; `eZPackage::fetch( $name )` without a repository returns
the first it finds, `local` first. Keep names unique across repositories.

## The local repository and the system repository

| Name | What it is | Type in the code |
|---|---|---|
| `local` | Always the first repository, created on demand; new packages go here | `local` |
| every other directory | One repository per vendor | `global` |
| the system repository | The repository named by `[RepositorySettings] Vendor` (`7x`): where the setup wizard looks for an offline `index.xml` | `eZPackage::systemRepositoryInformation()` |

The administration's package list shows the repositories and lets you switch between them; see
[The package list and package page](../admin-gui/the-package-list-and-package-page.md).

## The .cache directory

When the kernel reads a package, it writes the parsed definition to `<package>/.cache/package.php` and uses that copy
as long as it is not older than `package.xml` and was written by the same code version (`CACHE_CODE_DATE`). It is a
cache: deleting it is harmless, and it is never exported or archived (`exportToArchive()` copies only `documents`,
`files`, `simplefiles`, `settings` and the item directories). When you edit a `package.xml` in place, its newer time
stamp makes the kernel read it again.

## An offline index.xml

When the setup wizard or the kickstarter cannot download `<RemotePackagesIndexURL>/index.xml`, it copies
`var/storage/packages/<Vendor>/index.xml` (with `Vendor=7x`: `var/storage/packages/7x/index.xml`) and uses it instead
(`eZStepSiteTypes::retrieveRemotePackagesList()`). Combined with packages that are already imported, this allows an
install without network access:

```bash
# on a machine with access, from the installation root
curl -s -o var/storage/packages/7x/index.xml \
  https://exponential.packages.exponential.earth/exponential/6.0/6.0.15/index.xml
php ezpm.php import sevenx_multisite.ezpkg
php ezpm.php import sevenx_classes.ezpkg
php ezpm.php import sevenx_multisite_democontent.ezpkg
```

The `url` attributes in that index still point to the server, so every package a run needs must already be imported.
The full procedure, including mirrors, is in
[Offline installs and mirrors](../package-server/offline-installs-and-mirrors.md).

## What you may do by hand

| Action | Safe? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Copy a package directory into a repository | yes | Same as an import, without the archive checks; keep the directory name equal to `<name>` |
| Delete a `.cache/` directory | yes | It is written again |
| Delete a package directory | yes for the repository | Prefer **Remove** in Setup > Packages or `ezpm delete`: they also clear the installed record. What an install put on the site stays either way |
| Edit `package.xml` in place | with care | A broken definition hides the package. Make lasting changes in the package's source repository |
| Put a package in a directory that is not a repository | no | It is not found |
| Add symbolic links inside a package | no | The removal confirmation refuses a package whose directory contains a link |

> **Tip**
> `var/storage/packages/` belongs in your backups when you install offline or keep packages of your own there. The
> packages of the package server can be downloaded again at any time.
